assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, two orders better than caesium fountains. This is a clean, original instrument advance that opened a new measurement regime (relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants, a redefinition of the second).
assessment.attribution: Katori made the decisive conceptual proposal and first demonstration with strontium; Jun Ye's group drove the performance to the lowest systematic uncertainties and the many-body clock work. Two laureates is a natural, fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others) and now central to metrology roadmaps. Timely and mature.
uncertainties: Ion-clock pioneers and the broader frequency-comb lineage (partly recognised in 2005) could be argued as competing credit, though they are not on this entry.
Redefinition of the SI second has not yet happened, so the full practical payoff is still ahead.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a neutrino telescope and established the diffuse high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux, then the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane neutrino emission. A new observational window with a huge detector-engineering effort is the kind of discovery I value most.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project and its science case; Karle is credited for the detector construction and the central calibration and analysis work. Shigeru Yoshida is credited but I judge the case for him weaker than for the other two. With a collaboration of hundreds, a prize to two leaders risks being seen as incomplete; unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed at high significance and in multiple channels; the TXS blazar and NGC 1068 results are strong but single-source evidence, and ANTARES/KM3NeT/Baikal-GVD are only partially independent.
uncertainties: Origin of the bulk of the diffuse flux is still unresolved, so the interpretation is not yet stable.
Division of credit among Halzen, Karle, and early pioneers (AMANDA, DUMAND) is uncertain.
I cannot independently verify the exact significance of the latest source results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays gave evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, likely from supermassive black-hole binaries. It is a decades-long measurement built on millisecond-pulsar timing precision, opening a new gravitational-wave band. Strong physics and instrument value.
assessment.attribution: The three names map onto the three regional arrays (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA), which is one defensible configuration, but the discovery is a collective, multi-year effort and the theory of correlation (Hellings-Downs) and the pulsar-timing method have other originators not credited here. Attribution is genuinely difficult.
assessment.maturity: NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA and CPTA reported consistent evidence in 2023, but at about 2 to 4 sigma for the Hellings-Downs correlation; not yet a five-sigma detection. The source (supermassive black-hole binaries versus new physics) is not settled. Possibly premature.
uncertainties: Significance of the Hellings-Downs correlation is below discovery threshold in my recollection.
Credit allocation among arrays and individuals is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry underpins precision measurements of gravity, the gravitational constant, the fine-structure constant, inertial navigation and tests of the equivalence principle. A durable measurement technique with broad scientific and practical reach.
assessment.attribution: Bordé's early theory and Ramsey-Bordé interferometer, Pritchard's first matter-wave interferometer with atoms and Kasevich's precision gravimetry and gyroscopes form a coherent set. Steven Chu has already been honoured (1997) for cooling, and his interferometry credit overlaps, which could complicate the narrative.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and commercialised; large-scale gravitational-wave and dark-matter detection proposals depend on it. Mature, though the biggest fundamental-physics applications are still in development.
uncertainties: Overlap of credit with Chu, Chu-Kasevich group members and Cohen-Tannoudji lineage.
Whether the committee wants metrology prizes so close to the optical-clock topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BeppoSAX X-ray afterglow detection and the optical and redshift follow-up settled the 25-year debate on gamma-ray burst distances and showed they are cosmological. This is a decisive observational discovery enabled by an instrument (wide-field cameras plus narrow-field instruments), and it created a new field.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX GRB detection and localisation; Kulkarni's group delivered the optical, radio and redshift follow-up. Other major contributors are not on this entry (e.g. van Paradijs, Groot, Metzger, Djorgovski, and the Swift builders), so the configuration is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed thousands of times by Swift, Fermi, and gravitational-wave counterpart GW170817. Fully mature, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Competition for credit between X-ray and optical discovery teams and Swift's role.
The Nobel physics versus astronomy emphasis is a committee judgment I cannot settle alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuinely new semiconductor laser concept based on engineered intersubband transitions, giving compact mid-infrared and terahertz sources. It is original, invented rather than found, and widely used for gas sensing and spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Faist and Capasso, with Cho's molecular beam epitaxy growth in the 1994 Bell Labs demonstration, are the decisive trio on the entry; I would favour Capasso and Faist, noting that growth by Cho was essential and Kazarinov-Suris proposed intersubband gain in 1971.
assessment.maturity: Operating at room temperature and continuous wave since the early 2000s, with commercial products and a large community. Mature.
uncertainties: Earlier proposal by Kazarinov and Suris is not on the list and complicates priority.
Capasso also appears on the metamaterials entry, so allocation across entries could matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform for flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity. It transformed 2D materials and moire physics, with a clear prediction followed by striking experiments.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observations. The prediction-experiment pairing is clean, but the experiments depend on fabrication work by others.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, though the mechanism of superconductivity is still debated, so interpretation is not yet stable. Condensed matter is outside my expertise and I defer to colleagues on this ranking.
uncertainties: Other contributors to early moire theory (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell) are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter with protected edge or surface states. The theory is elegant and the experimental confirmation in HgTe wells and later bulk materials is solid, with lasting influence across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 theory; Molenkamp's group realised the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators are essential parts of the story, so a three-person configuration is hard to make fully fair.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by several independent groups and ARPES and transport; still timely. I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on relative priority.
uncertainties: Credit split between 2D and 3D topological insulators and the absent theorists.
Overlap with entries B003 and B020 on the quantum spin Hall and anomalous Hall effects.
